# Atlas Admin API rate limiting for scheduled polling — concept pack (small)

> Source-anchored research for Atlas Admin API rate limiting for scheduled polling. Run status: COMPLETED.

<!-- generated by llms-concept-abstractor v1.4.1 · generated 2026-10-31 · budgeted to ≈8000 tokens; the full catalogue is llms-full.txt -->

## Structure and components

- [statement] Schedule periodic polling with a stable per-worker offset to spread synchronized cron bursts, and cap retries at one layer; Amazon documents both practices from operational experience. (low confidence) — https://aws.amazon.com/builders-library/timeouts-retries-and-backoff-with-jitter/

## How it works

- [statement] After HTTP 429, honor Retry-After when present and apply exponential backoff with jitter; another client can exhaust the shared bucket before the retry. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/api/api-rate-limit.md · keywords: Atlas Admin API rate limiting for scheduled polling · also: https://aws.amazon.com/builders-library/timeouts-retries-and-backoff-with-jitter/

## How-to and procedures

- [statement] Use GET /api/atlas/v2/rateLimits with scope filters to inspect applicable policies; atlas api rateLimiting exposes listRateLimits and getRateLimit commands. Defaults can change without notice or differ after support adjustments. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/api/api-rate-limit.md · keywords: Atlas Admin API rate limiting for scheduled polling · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/cli/current/command/atlas-api-rateLimiting.md

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] Atlas V2 uses token buckets shared by endpoint set and resource scope; one uniform project-wide request limit does not describe the API. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/api/api-rate-limit.md
- [statement] RateLimit-Limit describes burst capacity, RateLimit-Remaining available tokens, and Retry-After a minimum delay in seconds after throttling; clients must tolerate absent headers. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/api/api-rate-limit.md
- [statement] Microsoft’s Atlas discovery integration distinguishes temporary rate-limit failures from authentication and permission failures, and lets users retry one credential without rechecking every credential. (low confidence) — https://microsoft.github.io/vscode-documentdb/user-manual/service-discovery-mongodb-atlas-troubleshooting
- [statement] MongoDB’s Terraform provider documents OAuth token acquisition returning 429 independently of resource calls; its troubleshooting guidance scopes this limit to the IP-address and Service Account client combination. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30) — https://github.com/mongodb/terraform-provider-mongodbatlas/blob/master/docs/guides/provider-configuration.md

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] Documented GROUP defaults are capacity 1200 and refill 500/60 seconds for Performance Advisor, including slowQueryLogs, versus capacity 300 and refill 100/60 seconds for Monitoring And Logs. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/api/api-rate-limit.md
- [statement] Mattering’s own Atlas integration reports HTTP 429 instead of silently retrying; its documentation recommends wait steps between bursts and spreading scheduled sweeps apart. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30) — https://www.mattering.io/documentation/automations/integrations/mongodb-atlas/

## Facts and statements

- [statement] Scheduling inference: budget aggregate poll requests, pagination and retries per endpoint set and project against refill rate; burst capacity is not sustained throughput. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/api/api-rate-limit.md · keywords: Atlas Admin API rate limiting for scheduled polling · also: https://aws.amazon.com/builders-library/timeouts-retries-and-backoff-with-jitter/
